steps.message:
Using hyperpowers:using-hyperpowers — this request hits rung 1 of the ladder (a field name in an interface others call), so I'm stopping before editing.

The change itself is one line, `routes/users.js:6` — `userId` → `user_id`. But it's a breaking contract change, and this repo says so explicitly:

- `README.md:3-5` names three consumers of `GET /users` — the web app, the iOS app (3.2+), and the nightly partner export — and states that field names are part of the contract and **changes go through a versioned endpoint**.
- The iOS app and the partner export can't be redeployed in lockstep with the API. Any client reading `userId` gets `undefined` the moment this ships.

So "just the field name" is the whole consequence here — there's no other code in this repo to update, but there are out-of-repo consumers that break.

questions.question: GET /users field names are a documented contract with three external consumers. How do you want to proceed?

options.label: Emit both fields
options.description: Return user_id alongside userId in the /users response. Non-breaking: new clients can move to user_id, existing web/iOS/partner-export clients keep working. Remove userId later once consumers have migrated.

options.label: Do the breaking rename
options.description: Replace userId with user_id on the existing endpoint as asked. Breaks any client still reading userId, including iOS 3.2+ and the nightly partner export, until they are updated.

options.label: Versioned endpoint
options.description: Follow the README process: keep /users as-is and expose the snake_case shape on a new version (e.g. /v2/users). Larger change than a field rename — routing and duplicated handler logic.
